'The vendor tracker and the newsletter,' said Minakshi, sliding the folder across. 'Those are the two I'm handing over. Everything's documented.'
'And you're really taking the full two weeks?' said Damini.
'I've got leave piled up from a year I never used. I'm using it.'
'What about when you're back?'
'I've asked our manager to cut my load for a month and bring the work back gradually. Half of what I did before, for the first two weeks.'
'Honestly? I was wondering when you'd stop.' Damini opened the folder. 'I'll cover them. Just make sure your phone isn't in your bag.'
'It's switched off.' Minakshi laughed, a small tired sound. 'I'm going to sleep for three days.'

qa.a: Damini seems willing and supportive, having wondered when Minakshi would stop, though the extra work may still be a lot.

subtype: Approach: taking planned leave and reducing load [Action]
passage:
I had nineteen days of leave sitting unused, and I'd stopped being able to read a whole email without drifting. So in February I made a list and took it to Nirmala, my manager, instead of just sighing at my desk.
First: two weeks' leave from the 10th. Second: I'd hand over the vendor audit to Pooja and the training rollout to Imtiaz, with a handover note each, before going. Third, and this was the hard one to say aloud: when I came back, could I have a lighter month? Only my own project, and no new work until April.
Nirmala read it twice and said yes to all three. "Reena, I'd rather have you back slowly than not at all," she said. The handovers took two long days. The leave felt strange for the first four days, then good. Coming back to half a load was the part that actually helped.

qa.q: Who took over the vendor audit?
qa.a: Pooja took over the vendor audit.

qa.q: Why was the third request the hard one for Reena to say aloud?
qa.a: Reena felt embarrassed and a little afraid that asking for a lighter month would look weak or uncommitted.

qa.q: What would you change first if the handovers had not been ready in time?
qa.a: Reena could ask Nirmala to move the leave start by a few days rather than leave without handover notes.

qa.q: How might Pooja and Imtiaz see the handovers?
qa.a: They take on extra work but also get clear notes, so they can likely manage without calling Reena on leave.

grounding: It shows someone using saved leave, handing two projects to colleagues and asking the manager for a lighter month and a gradual restart.

subtype: Approach: taking planned leave and reducing load [Action]
passage:
Supervisor's note, 28 May.
Binita asked for a meeting this morning and came with everything written down. She has 22 days of leave saved and wants to use 15 of them from 3 June, because she is "running on fumes". Her two open projects: the clinic survey goes to Jyoti, the data clean-up to Farooq. She has written handover notes for both and booked half an hour with each of them.
She also asked that when she returns, she works on only one project for four weeks and joins meetings in the afternoons only for the first week. I said yes. I will tell the team on Friday that her return is gradual and that new requests should not go to her until July.
She looked relieved and said, "I didn't think you'd agree to all of it." I will check in with her after her first week back.

qa.q: Who is taking the clinic survey?
qa.a: Jyoti is taking the clinic survey.

qa.q: What did Binita feel when the supervisor agreed?
qa.a: Binita looked relieved and a little surprised, having expected at least part of the request to be turned down 😊

qa.q: What else could support Binita's gradual restart?
qa.a: The check-in after her first week back could be used to decide together whether to add a second project or keep the load light for longer.

qa.q: How might Jyoti experience taking over the clinic survey?
qa.a: Jyoti gains extra work but also a written handover and a half-hour meeting, which makes the change manageable.

grounding: It shows a woman using saved leave, handing over two projects and asking for a reduced load and gradual restart on her return.
